questions.text: All mutual fund distributors must hold a valid registration with:
questions.explanation: Distributors must obtain AMFI Registration Number (ARN) after completing the NISM Mutual Fund Distributors certification.

questions.text: PoA holders can redeem mutual fund units only if:
options: It is specifically authorized in the PoA document
AMC permits all PoA redemptions automatically
Units are held in physical form only
questions.explanation: Redemption authority must be explicitly stated in the Power of Attorney document.

questions.text: In a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP), the main benefit arising from investing a fixed amount at regular intervals is called:
questions.explanation: SIPs enable rupee cost averaging, where the investor buys more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, reducing average cost per unit over time.

questions.text: Front-running is an unethical practice where:
options: Advisor trades on own account ahead of executing a large client order
Trades are done only in front-office hours
questions.explanation: Front-running occurs when an intermediary uses prior knowledge of a big client order to trade for personal gain first.

questions.text: Which statement about equity SIPs (Systematic Investment Plans) is TRUE?
options: They involve investing fixed amounts at regular intervals, averaging purchase cost over time
They guarantee positive returns in the short term
They are available only to HNIs
questions.explanation: Equity SIPs help average purchase cost by investing periodically, but do not remove market risk.

questions.text: As the number of securities in a portfolio increases, the number of covariance terms:
questions.explanation: For n securities, the number of covariance terms is n(n–1)/2, which grows rapidly as portfolio size increases.

questions.text: Tax considerations affect portfolio construction because:
options: Different types of income are taxed differently
Taxes have no impact on net returns
Investors can ignore capital gains tax
questions.explanation: Interest, dividends, and capital gains are taxed differently; hence tax planning affects net portfolio returns.

questions.text: In equity derivatives, the lot size is:
options: Fixed by SEBI for all stocks
Standardised and notified by exchanges for each contract
questions.explanation: Lot size is standardised by exchanges to ensure uniform contract trading units.

questions.text: Earnings Per Share (EPS) is:
options: Net profit ÷ number of equity shares
questions.explanation: EPS = Profit after tax ÷ weighted average number of equity shares.

questions.text: A puttable bond:
options: Allows the issuer to repay early at a lower price
Allows the investor to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-specified price on certain dates
questions.explanation: Puttable bonds give bondholders the right to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-set price, reducing interest rate risk for investors.

questions.text: Which is the most appropriate reason for young earners to start investing early?
options: They can benefit from compounding over a longer period
questions.explanation: Starting early allows investments more time to compound, significantly increasing the eventual corpus.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers can invest a maximum of ___% of a client’s portfolio in their own associate or related companies.
questions.explanation: As per SEBI, the cap is 30% with prior written consent from the client.

questions.text: Which represents revolving credit?
questions.explanation: Revolving credit allows re-borrowing up to the limit as payments are made.

questions.text: Reducing interest rate but extending tenure on loan will generally:
options: Increase EMI and reduce total interest
Reduce EMI but may increase total interest paid
Reduce both EMI and total interest
questions.explanation: Longer tenure means lower monthly payment but higher cumulative interest.

questions.text: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: Portfolio Management Services are governed by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the earlier 1993 regulations.

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: Inflation risk for a fixed rate bond investor is:
options: Risk that inflation will fall and real returns rise
Risk that higher inflation erodes the real purchasing power of fixed coupon and principal
Risk that bond cannot be redeemed at par
Risk that bond will be converted into equity
questions.explanation: If inflation rises, the real (inflation-adjusted) value of fixed coupons and principal declines, which is inflation risk.

questions.text: Retirement funds and children’s funds launched by mutual funds are classified as:
questions.explanation: Retirement funds and children’s funds fall under SEBI’s solution-oriented scheme category and come with specified lock-in periods.

questions.text: Downgrade risk refers to:
options: Risk that rating agencies may upgrade the bond, reducing yield
Risk that the bond’s credit rating is lowered after purchase, causing its market price to fall
Risk that interest rates will fall
Risk that the bond cannot be listed
questions.explanation: If a rating agency downgrades an issuer, investors demand higher yield, causing existing bond prices to fall—this is downgrade risk.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid KYC document for proof of identity?
questions.explanation: Electricity bill is acceptable as proof of address, not as proof of identity.

questions.text: Account statement for mutual fund investments must be dispatched within:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that account statements be sent within 7 business days from the date of transaction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about asset allocation is TRUE?
options: It has minimal impact on portfolio performance
It is the key determinant of long-term portfolio returns and risk
It focuses only on stock selection
It can be ignored once the portfolio is constructed
questions.explanation: Empirical studies show asset allocation is the major driver of a portfolio’s long-term risk and return.

questions.text: Borrowing to purchase consumables or luxury goods is generally termed:
questions.explanation: Such borrowing doesn’t create assets or future income.

questions.text: Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, a mutual fund is constituted as:
questions.explanation: Every mutual fund is set up as a trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, with the sponsor, trustees, and AMC as constituents.

questions.text: For mutual fund-related complaints, investors can also contact:
questions.explanation: AMFI assists investors in resolving mutual fund-related complaints in coordination with the concerned AMC.

questions.text: Which asset class is generally considered most suitable for capital preservation with modest returns over the short term?
options: Structured products linked to equity indices
questions.explanation: Liquid and short-term debt instruments usually focus on capital preservation and modest returns.

questions.text: Money-weighted rate of return is also known as:
questions.explanation: Money-weighted return is the internal rate of return (IRR) that equates the present value of cash inflows and outflows.

questions.text: Dividends paid on equity shares are:
options: Discretionary and depend on company profits
questions.explanation: Equity dividends are not fixed; the board declares them based on profits and policy.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: If monthly income ₹1 lakh and total EMIs ₹35,000, DTI ratio is:
A decrease in net worth may be due to:
questions.explanation: Borrowing or fall in asset values can reduce net worth.

questions.text: The primary regulator for mutual funds in India is:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates mutual funds under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 and subsequent amendments.

questions.text: Which of these is a constraint that may affect personal financial planning?
questions.explanation: Income, responsibilities and the regulatory framework all act as constraints that the plan must consider.

questions.text: ‘Putting client money in schemes that advisor personally likes, ignoring IPS’ is primarily a breach of:
questions.explanation: Ignoring the client’s Investment Policy Statement (IPS) violates fiduciary duty and suitability of advice.

questions.text: Investors must update change in address or bank details:
questions.explanation: KYC-linked changes such as address and bank details must be updated with the KRA, which auto-updates all linked AMCs.

questions.text: Inspection of intermediaries by SEBI is conducted to:
options: Ensure compliance with laws and regulations
questions.explanation: SEBI inspects intermediaries to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and investor protection norms.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: Which statement about personal financial planning is TRUE?
options: It is a one-time exercise done at the start of a career
It needs periodic review and updating as life circumstances change
It only applies to high-net-worth individuals
It is relevant only close to retirement
questions.explanation: Financial planning is a dynamic process and needs regular review as income, family situation and goals change.

questions.text: A borrower takes ₹5 lakh for 5 years at 10% p.a. monthly compounding. The EMI is closest to:
questions.explanation: Using EMI formula, r = 0.10/12, n = 60 ⇒ EMI ≈ ₹10,624.

questions.text: In an interest rate futures contract, the underlying is typically:
options: A government security or interest rate benchmark
questions.explanation: Interest rate futures are based on government securities or reference interest rate benchmarks.

questions.text: Why should irregular income (like bonuses) be treated carefully in budgeting?
options: It may not occur regularly and shouldn’t fund fixed commitments
It should always be spent fully
questions.explanation: Irregular income is uncertain and best used for one-time goals or debt reduction.

questions.text: The sequence in which mutual fund units are held jointly determines:
options: The tax liability of each holder
Whose signature is required for redemption
questions.explanation: The sequence determines signature order, redemption rights, and nomination applicability for joint holders.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about standard deviation in portfolio theory?
options: It measures the average return of a portfolio
It measures dispersion of returns around the mean
It is always equal to variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and measures the dispersion of returns around the mean.

questions.text: The most widely used risk-adjusted performance measure is:
questions.explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is the most popular risk-adjusted performance measure, assessing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: Rematerialisation refers to:
options: Conversion of electronic holdings into physical certificates
Buying shares in the secondary market
Transfer of ownership in electronic form
questions.explanation: Rematerialisation is converting demat holdings back into physical share certificates.

questions.text: Which document lists all loans and credit cards held by an individual?
questions.explanation: CIBIL or credit report shows all borrowings and repayment history.

questions.text: An annuity is:
options: A series of equal payments made at regular intervals
questions.explanation: An annuity involves equal periodic payments or receipts.

questions.text: Which regulator primarily oversees the securities and commodity derivatives markets in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI is the statutory regulator for the securities market and commodity derivatives market.

questions.text: In the insurance market, which entities sell products of one or more insurers to customers?
questions.explanation: Insurance brokers and corporate agents distribute insurance products; brokers can offer products from multiple insurers.

questions.text: Stock market indices such as Nifty 50 or Sensex are designed to:
questions.explanation: Stock indices serve as barometers of market performance.

questions.text: The best indicator of over-borrowing is:
questions.explanation: DTI above 40% suggests too much income going toward debt.

questions.text: For a home loan, lenders generally prefer LTV below:
questions.explanation: Banks usually lend up to 75–80% of property value.

questions.text: Demat-based transactions in mutual funds are settled on:
questions.explanation: Exchange-traded mutual fund units follow T+2 rolling settlement cycles similar to equity transactions.

questions.text: In which stage of the financial life cycle does preservation of capital and regular income become more important than high growth?
questions.explanation: As individuals near retirement, their focus shifts to capital preservation and stable income.

questions.text: Balance transfer of loan means:
options: Transferring EMI payment to another person
Shifting loan to another lender offering better terms
questions.explanation: Balance transfer helps take advantage of lower interest or better service.

questions.text: Insider trading is best described as:
options: Using unpublished price-sensitive information for personal gain
questions.explanation: Insider trading involves using unpublished price-sensitive information, violating fairness and regulations.

questions.text: A repo (repurchase agreement) transaction is essentially:
options: A collateralised borrowing by selling securities with an agreement to repurchase later
A permanent sale of securities in the secondary market
questions.explanation: Repo is a collateralised borrowing: the borrower sells securities today and agrees to repurchase them later at a higher price reflecting interest.

questions.text: Which document must a PMS provide to clients before onboarding?
questions.explanation: The PMS must furnish a Disclosure Document detailing fees, risks, related-party transactions, and performance.

questions.text: Which ministry is responsible for macroeconomic policy and capital markets through its Department of Economic Affairs?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance, via the Department of Economic Affairs, handles macroeconomic policy and capital markets.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: Diversification helps primarily to reduce:
questions.explanation: Diversification reduces company-specific (unsystematic) risk but not market-wide (systematic) risk.

questions.text: If a borrower prepays part of the principal early in a reducing-balance loan, future interest cost:
questions.explanation: Prepayment lowers outstanding principal, thereby reducing future interest.

questions.text: Portfolio performance evaluation primarily aims to:
options: Measure only the total return of the portfolio
Assess both the return earned and the risk undertaken
Compare the portfolio with random market indices
questions.explanation: Performance evaluation measures both risk and return to determine whether the portfolio met its objectives relative to benchmarks.

questions.text: Dematerialisation refers to:
options: Conversion of physical share certificates into electronic form
questions.explanation: Dematerialisation converts paper share certificates into electronic holdings in a demat account.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about personal financial planning is FALSE?
options: It helps in managing income and expenses better
It encourages disciplined saving and investing
It replaces the need for budgeting
It links investments to specific goals
questions.explanation: Financial planning does not replace budgeting; budgeting is an important tool within the overall plan.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, an AMC can offer:
options: Both a value fund and a contra fund
Only a value fund but not a contra fund
Only a contra fund but not a value fund
Either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both
questions.explanation: A mutual fund house can have either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both, as per SEBI categorisation norms.

questions.text: The expiration day for equity derivatives in India is generally:
options: Last Thursday of the expiry month
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives on NSE and BSE typically expire on the last Thursday of the contract month.

questions.text: The primary risk associated with investing in equities is:
options: Market volatility and loss of capital
questions.explanation: Equities are subject to market risk — price fluctuations due to company and economic factors.

questions.text: An ethical response, if a mistake is made in executing client instructions, is to:
options: Hide the error and hope markets recover
Promptly disclose the error, correct it, and compensate where required
questions.explanation: Honesty and accountability require disclosure of mistakes, corrective action, and fair compensation if client suffers loss.

questions.text: Over-leveraging occurs when:
options: Liabilities are disproportionately high compared to income or assets
questions.explanation: Excessive borrowing relative to capacity leads to financial strain.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a lifestyle goal?
options: Owning a bigger car within 3 years
Paying off credit card dues this month
questions.explanation: Lifestyle goals relate to a desired standard of living, such as owning a bigger car or a better house.

questions.text: An intermediary found guilty of mis-selling or misconduct may face:
options: Suspension or cancellation of registration by SEBI
Tax penalty by Income Tax Department
questions.explanation: SEBI can suspend, cancel, or impose monetary penalties on intermediaries violating regulations.

questions.text: Small-cap funds are required to invest at least 65% of their total assets in:
options: Companies ranked 251 and above by market capitalisation
questions.explanation: Small-cap companies are defined as those ranked 251 onwards by full market capitalisation, and small-cap funds must invest at least 65% in them.

questions.text: The slope of the Capital Market Line equals:
options: Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio
questions.explanation: The slope of the CML is the Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio, representing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: Which of the following investors are eligible to invest in AIFs?
options: Resident, NRI and foreign investors, subject to FEMA
questions.explanation: AIFs can accept investment from resident, NRI and foreign investors in compliance with FEMA and SEBI norms.

questions.text: Call risk is associated with:
options: Bonds that may be redeemed by the issuer before maturity
Bonds that cannot be sold in the secondary market
Bonds with very long maturities only
questions.explanation: Call risk arises in callable bonds where the issuer may redeem early, forcing the investor to reinvest at possibly lower yields.

questions.text: Which of the following small saving instruments is specifically targeted at the girl child?
questions.explanation: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account is a long-term small savings scheme specifically designed for the benefit of the girl child.

questions.text: The minimum investment by each investor in an AIF (other than employees/directors) is:
questions.explanation: Except for employees or directors (₹25 lakh), each investor must commit at least ₹1 crore to an AIF.

questions.text: Units in a folio with joint holders are transmitted to:
questions.explanation: In joint holdings, upon the death of one holder, the units are transmitted to the surviving holder(s).

questions.text: Category II AIFs typically comprise:
options: Private-equity and debt funds that do not employ leverage
Hedge funds using complex trading strategies
Angel networks investing less than ₹10 lakh
questions.explanation: Category II AIFs are private-equity or debt funds that do not undertake leverage other than for day-to-day operational requirements.

questions.text: A Portfolio Manager as per SEBI regulations is defined as:
options: Any individual who advises investors occasionally
A body corporate managing client funds or securities under a contract
A mutual fund distributor selling schemes
questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager is a body corporate that, under a contract with a client, manages or administers a portfolio of securities or funds on behalf of the client as per SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.

questions.text: Which is the MOST suitable investment for parking an emergency fund?
options: Liquid mutual fund or savings bank account
questions.explanation: Emergency funds must be readily accessible and low risk, so liquid funds or savings accounts are appropriate.

questions.text: A mutual fund is best described as:
options: A bank account where money is kept only in cash
An investment vehicle that pools money from investors to invest in a portfolio of securities
A company that gives fixed deposits with guaranteed returns
A government savings scheme with fixed interest
questions.explanation: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a portfolio of securities such as equity, debt or gold, managed by an AMC.

questions.text: The efficient frontier represents:
options: The set of portfolios with the highest return for a given level of risk
The set of portfolios with the lowest return and highest risk
All possible combinations of risky and risk-free assets
questions.explanation: The efficient frontier shows the optimal portfolios that provide maximum expected return for a given risk or minimum risk for a given return.

questions.text: Which statement about diversification is correct in personal finance?
options: It spreads investments across different assets to reduce unsystematic risk
questions.explanation: Diversification helps reduce unsystematic risk by spreading investments, but it cannot eliminate market risk.

questions.text: A derivative is a financial instrument whose value is derived from:
options: An underlying asset such as a stock, bond, commodity or index
questions.explanation: A derivative’s price depends on the value or performance of an underlying asset such as equity, bond, commodity, currency or index.

questions.text: Registrar and Transfer Agents (RTAs) primarily:
options: Maintain investor records, handle transactions and corporate actions for issuers and mutual funds
questions.explanation: RTAs maintain investor registers and handle back-office processes like transfers, redemptions and corporate action processing.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations correctly matches asset class and its typical characteristic?
options: Government bond – low credit risk, interest rate risk present
Real estate – highly liquid, intraday tradable
questions.explanation: Government bonds usually have low credit risk, but their prices are still affected by changes in interest rates.

questions.text: A change in mode of holding (single to joint) in a mutual fund folio:
options: Is allowed with consent of all parties
Is not permitted; a new folio must be created
questions.explanation: Change in mode of holding is not allowed in existing folios; a new folio must be created with the new configuration.

questions.text: Should he take this loan?
questions.explanation: Borrowing for non-productive expense at high DTI is poor financial decision.

questions.text: A better choice would be to:

questions.text: His high DTI also affects:
questions.explanation: Higher debt burden and missed EMIs can lower credit rating.
